answer: Every head runs on one hardware-attested host key that signs each pulse it relays; at each dawn the host signs its roster of heads whose pulses it carried, the ledger records that roster and locks every listed head's epoch burn at base times the roster size, paid in ivory — no clone can hop hosts mid-epoch to dodge a price fixed at the last dawn. An operator packing k clones on one host burns base×k per clone, k²×base per epoch, each added clone raising every clone's burn; spreading out means one attested TEE per clone, capital not rentable in bulk. A lone head burns base.
